name: Picpoul de Pinet

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Grenache, Carignan, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sangiovese and Zinfandel fully without cooking off their freshness.
Grenache and Carignan sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Syrah is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Merlot is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Sand is warm and airy. It drains fast but holds little water, and phylloxera does not thrive in it. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
